title: Nanotechnology Engineering Technologists and Technicians
description: Implement production processes and operate commercial-scale production equipment to produce, test, or modify materials, devices, or systems of unique molecular or macromolecular composition. Operate advanced microscopy equipment to manipulate nanoscale objects. Work under the supervision of nanoengineering staff.

tasks.text: Maintain accurate record or batch-record documentation of nanoproduction.
Prepare capability data, training materials, or other documentation for transfer of processes to production.
Prepare detailed verbal or written presentations for scientists, engineers, project managers, or upper management.
Contribute written material or data for grant or patent applications.
Assist nanoscientists or engineers in writing process specifications or documentation.
Collaborate with scientists or engineers to design or conduct experiments for the development of nanotechnology materials, components, devices, or systems.
Collect or compile nanotechnology research or engineering data.
Measure emission of nanodust or nanoparticles during nanocomposite or other nano-scale production processes, using systems such as aerosol detection systems.
Compare the performance or environmental impact of nanomaterials by nanoparticle size, shape, or organization.
Analyze the life cycle of nanomaterials or nano-enabled products to determine environmental impact.

clusters.label: Estimating the Quantifiable Characteristics of Products, Events, or Information

tasks.text: Produce images or measurements, using tools or techniques such as atomic force microscopy, scanning electron microscopy, optical microscopy, particle size analysis, or zeta potential analysis.
Assist nanoscientists or engineers in processing or characterizing materials according to physical or chemical properties.
Inspect or measure thin films of carbon nanotubes, polymers, or inorganic coatings, using a variety of techniques or analytical tools.
Calibrate nanotechnology equipment, such as weighing, testing, or production equipment.
Measure or mix chemicals or compounds in accordance with detailed instructions or formulas.
Assemble components, using techniques such as interference fitting, solvent bonding, adhesive bonding, heat sealing, or ultrasonic welding.
Monitor hazardous waste cleanup procedures to ensure proper application of nanocomposites or accomplishment of objectives.
Monitor equipment during operation to ensure adherence to specifications for characteristics such as pressure, temperature, or flow.

Operate nanotechnology compounding, testing, processing, or production equipment in accordance with appropriate standard operating procedures, good manufacturing practices, hazardous material restrictions, or health and safety requirements.
Process nanoparticles or nanostructures, using technologies such as ultraviolet radiation, microwave energy, or catalysis.
Maintain work area according to cleanroom or other processing standards.
Repair nanotechnology processing or testing equipment or submit work orders for equipment repair.
Implement new or enhanced methods or processes for the processing, testing, or manufacture of nanotechnology materials or products.
Develop or modify wet chemical or industrial laboratory experimental techniques for nanoscale use.
Perform functional tests of nano-enhanced assemblies, components, or systems, using equipment such as torque gauges or conductivity meters.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Science
skills.def: Using scientific rules and methods to solve problems.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Operations Monitoring
skills.def: Watching gauges, dials, or other indicators to make sure a machine is working properly.

skills.name: Troubleshooting
skills.def: Determining causes of operating errors and deciding what to do about it.

skills.name: Systems Analysis
skills.def: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Mathematics
skills.def: Using mathematics to solve problems.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Repairing
skills.def: Repairing machines or systems using the needed tools.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Operation and Control
skills.def: Controlling operations of equipment or systems.

skills.name: Equipment Maintenance
skills.def: Performing routine maintenance on equipment and determining when and what kind of maintenance is needed.

skills.name: Quality Control Analysis
skills.def: Conducting tests and inspections of products, services, or processes to evaluate quality or performance.

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: Microsoft Access.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Presentation software
skills.def: Software to create presentations, speeches, or slideshows. Examples: Microsoft PowerPoint.

skills.name: Operating system software
skills.def: Software to provide the operational interface to a computer and provide higher-level services and APIs. Examples: Microsoft Windows.

skills.name: Word processing software
skills.def: Software to create, edit, store, or print documents. Examples: Microsoft Word.
